blogs.title: Why Orthogonal Finetuning Needs Butterfly – An Easy‑to‑Understand Primer
blogs.description: Demystify what it means to keep neurons’ angles the same when adapting a huge model, why the original OFT method ends up with a lot of trainable bits, and how the classic butterfly pattern from the fast Fourier transform offers a slick, sparse way to make a dense orthogonal matrix with far fewer parameters. Ideal for readers new to model adaptation and linear algebra.

blogs.title: Butterfly Structures vs. Block‑Diagonal: The Graphic Lens of Parameter Efficiency
blogs.description: Walk through the information‑transmission view introduced in the paper, using a simple grid diagram to show how different sparsity patterns—block‑diagonal vs. butterfly—affect how information flows between neurons. Readers will see why a carefully designed sparse network can transmit as much as a full matrix without all the extra trainable knobs.

blogs.title: BOFT in Action: From Vision Transformers to Text‑to‑Image Diffusion
blogs.description: Illustrate the wide‑range experiments—from image classification to language tasks and generative art—where Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning (BOFT) outperforms other parameter‑efficient methods. The post will highlight what really changes under the hood when you switch from OFT to BOFT.

blogs.title: The Trade‑off Between Expressivity and Generalization in Finetuning
blogs.description: Explore the theory that more expressive weight updates (full orthogonal matrices) can hurt generalization, while a structured subset like the butterfly offers a sweet spot. This blog will translate the paper’s theorem and experiments into plain language about over‑fitting, inductive bias, and why simple patterns often win.

blogs.title: FAQ & Myths About Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning
blogs.description: Address common questions—Does BOFT slow down inference? How does it compare to LoRA or adapters? What are the practical limits and best‑practice tips for tuning the block size and depth? The post will debunk myths and give a quick cheat‑sheet for practitioners.
